name: Build and test
on: [push, pull_request]
permissions:
  contents: read
jobs:
  macos:
    runs-on: macos-14
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable
        with:
          components: rustfmt, clippy
      - run: cargo fmt --check
      - run: cargo test --locked
      - run: cargo clippy --locked -- -D warnings
      - run: ./scripts/build.sh
      - run: python3 tests/recovery_check.py
      - run: python3 -m py_compile scripts/manage.py scripts/hardware_check.py

# Validation

Initial release validation: 2026-10-27, one Apple M5 Pro Mac on macOS 27.0, two Apple Studio Displays at 48 kHz. This is a beta, not a broad compatibility or listening-quality study.

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Rust routing, swapped channels, interleaved/planar layouts | Passed |
| Silent warmup and invalid buffer rejection | Passed |
| Nonfinite/bounded samples and gain ramp | Passed |
| Completed journal cannot signal a reused PID | Passed; failed on the old implementation |
| Same path but different process start time cannot be signalled | Passed; failed on the old implementation |
| Incomplete live legacy identity is refused | Passed; failed on the old implementation |
| Non-object journal reports an error without signalling | Passed; old implementation crashed |
| Real CoreAudio route: normal stop, forced worker death + restore, finite duration, continuous mode | Passed on the test setup |
| Continuous mode | Survived the short test, then stopped on request; no long-duration claim |
| Defaults, sample rates and secondary controls after those runs | Returned to captured baseline |
| Native left/right swap and pairing switch | Observed working |
| Controller recovers from killed audio worker | Passed with Spotify playing |
| Quit/relaunch preserves assignment, pairing and login | Passed |
| Source installer upgrade and uninstall | Passed; uninstall removed bundle, unregistered login and restored journal |
| Menu-bar launch at login registration | Enabled in macOS; actual reboot not tested |
| Deployment target | Both app and engine Mach-O load commands report macOS 14.2 |
| Signing | Ad hoc signature verified; not Developer ID signed or notarized |

The hardware runner uses its own quiet stereo source to isolate the route. Separately, Spotify playback reached **Stereo active** in the native app. Neither is a measurement of acoustic phase, latency, room response or subjective quality.

CI covers formatting, Rust tests, Clippy, a native app build and process-recovery regressions. It does not exercise hardware, audio permissions, menu interaction or login.

Still unverified: macOS 14.2 hardware behavior, Intel Macs, actual reboot startup, sleep/wake, display unplug/reconnect, Spotify upgrades, long sessions and acoustic synchronization. Unsupported layouts fail closed. Please report macOS version and redacted failure text, not raw journals or device inventories.

[package]
name = "studio-pair-engine"
version = "0.2.0"
edition = "2021"
rust-version = "1.87"
build = "build.rs"

[profile.release]
panic = "abort"
opt-level = 2

# Studio Pair **Two Studio Displays. One stereo pair. Your volume keys still work.** Studio Pair sends Spotify's left channel to one Apple Studio Display and its right channel to the other. A small native macOS menu-bar app lets you swap sides, turn pairing off, and launch at login. **Early beta. Spotify desktop only.** Other apps keep their normal output. Tested on one Apple silicon Mac with two Studio Displays. This is stereo routing; it does not add Dolby Atmos or guarantee better sound in every room. ## Install with your coding agent Paste into Codex or Claude Code: ```text Install Studio Pair from https://github.com/browser-use/studio-pair. Read install.md, check the prerequisites, build it locally, and install it in my user Applications folder. Preserve my audio defaults, volume, microphone, and existing settings. Show me the menu-bar controls and how to undo it. Ask before installing missing development tools. Do not run the hardware tone checks unless I ask. ``` Or, with Xcode Command Line Tools, Rust 1.87+ and Python 3 already installed: ```sh git clone https://github.com/browser-use/studio-pair.git cd studio-pair python3 scripts/manage.py install ``` Requires macOS 14.2+, Spotify desktop, and exactly two Studio Displays exposing eight-channel audio at 48 kHz. Select one Studio Display as your normal sound output, start Spotify, then open Studio Pair. macOS may ask for system audio capture permission. Enable **Launch at login** in the popover if you want it to start automatically. Builds are local and ad hoc signed. There is no notarized download yet. See [install.md](install.md) for setup and recovery. ## Turn it off Switch **Stereo pairing** off in the menu bar. Direct Spotify playback returns. Quit also stops the route; the app remembers your pairing preference for its next launch. ```sh python3 scripts/manage.py stop ``` Unregister launch at login, restore audio and remove the installed app: ```sh python3 scripts/manage.py uninstall ``` Settings and local recovery metadata are retained. No audio driver is installed. ## How it works ```text Spotify → private CoreAudio process tap → Rust audio callback ├─ left → Studio Display A └─ right → Studio Display B Native volume / mute on the selected display → mirrored to the second ``` - Swift/AppKit menu bar, Rust audio engine, Objective-C CoreAudio bridge. - Private aggregate with clock drift correction. Left/right assignment is saved by device identity. - No changes to default output, microphone or hardware sample rates. - A rollback journal tracks secondary volume/mute. Recovery restores those values only if they still match the app's last write. - No audio files, telemetry, network calls, third-party Rust crates or HAL driver. ## Limits and contributing The first release handles Spotify only. It needs a Studio Display as the default output, so switching to headphones returns Spotify to direct playback. Unsupported channel layouts or sample rates are rejected. The route uses -6 dB software headroom, so compare sound at matched listening volume. Clock drift correction is enabled and checked; acoustic synchronization has not been measured. Sleep/wake, unplug/reconnect, reboot login and long listening sessions still need broader testing. The macOS 14.2 deployment target is compiled in; actual hardware testing was on macOS 27.0. [Architecture and recovery](docs/architecture.md) · [Validation](docs/validation.md) · [Contributing](CONTRIBUTING.md) MIT licensed. Built for a two-display desk that should have been a stereo system already.

"""Recovery must not signal a recycled PID. Uses disposable sleep processes, no audio."""
import json
import os
from pathlib import Path
import subprocess
import tempfile
import unittest

ENGINE = Path(os.environ.get('STUDIO_PAIR_ENGINE_PATH', Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1] / 'build/Studio Pair.app/Contents/MacOS/studio-pair-engine'))


class RecoveryTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def check_recovery(self, restored=False, birth=None, valid=True):
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as directory:
            victim = subprocess.Popen(['/bin/sleep', '30'])
            try:
                journal = dict(pid=victim.pid, executable='/bin/sleep', restored=restored,
                               volume_written=False, mute_written=False)
                if birth is not None:
                    journal['process_birth'] = birth
                path = Path(directory) / 'journal.json'
                path.write_text(json.dumps(journal if valid else []))
                result = subprocess.run([str(ENGINE), 'restore', str(path)], capture_output=True, timeout=10)
                self.assertIsNone(victim.poll(), 'Recovery killed a process it did not own')
                return result.returncode, result.stderr.decode()
            finally:
                victim.terminate()
                victim.wait(timeout=3)

    def test_completed_journal_never_signals_saved_pid(self):
        self.assertEqual(self.check_recovery(restored=True)[0], 0)

    def test_recycled_pid_with_same_executable_survives(self):
        self.assertEqual(self.check_recovery(birth='0:0')[0], 0)

    def test_live_legacy_identity_requires_manual_quit(self):
        code, error = self.check_recovery()
        self.assertNotEqual(code, 0)
        self.assertIn('Legacy worker identity', error)

    def test_non_object_journal_fails_without_signalling(self):
        code, error = self.check_recovery(valid=False)
        self.assertNotEqual(code, 0)
        self.assertIn('Invalid rollback journal', error)


if __name__ == '__main__':
    unittest.main()

# Install and undo

Studio Pair is an early source-built macOS utility for Spotify desktop and two Apple Studio Displays. It is not affiliated with Apple or Spotify.

## Prerequisites

- macOS 14.2 or later. Apple silicon hardware tested; Intel hardware untested.
- Exactly two Studio Displays with eight output channels each, already at 48 kHz.
- Spotify desktop, playing through one Studio Display as the normal output.
- Xcode Command Line Tools, Rust 1.87+ with Cargo, and Python 3. Install missing tools only with the user's permission. Studio Pair's installer does not download tools.

## Build and install

```sh
git clone https://github.com/browser-use/studio-pair.git
cd studio-pair
python3 scripts/manage.py install
```

The installer compiles locally, verifies its ad hoc code signature, and places the app at `~/Applications/Studio Pair.app`. On upgrade it gracefully stops the existing app and keeps one previous bundle under `build/previous/`. An unrelated app at that path is never replaced. No `sudo` is needed.

Open the speaker-pair icon in the menu bar. Allow macOS system audio capture when prompted; this lets CoreAudio route Spotify's output. Audio stays in memory on this Mac. If permission was denied, enable Studio Pair under System Settings > Privacy & Security > Screen & System Audio Recording (the label varies by macOS version), then quit and reopen it.

Use the swap button if left/right is reversed. The app cannot infer the physical arrangement of your desk. Enable **Launch at login** if desired; macOS may require approval in Login Items.

The app does not change your sound output for you. If it says it is waiting for Studio Display output, choose one of your Studio Displays in macOS Sound settings. If it reports an unsupported layout/rate, leave pairing off. Hardware layouts beyond the tested 8+8 channels at 48 kHz need separate validation.

## Stop or uninstall

Use the pairing switch or **Quit Studio Pair**. Command-line recovery:

```sh
python3 scripts/manage.py stop
```

To unregister login, stop and restore audio, then remove the installed bundle:

```sh
python3 scripts/manage.py uninstall
```

The uninstall stops if recovery or login removal fails. Reconnect a missing display and retry. It retains preferences and `~/Library/Application Support/StudioPair` for recovery; those files contain device identities and should not be attached to public issues.

If the menu is unresponsive, quit the app with Activity Monitor, then run the stop command. Recovery checks both executable path and process start time before signalling a saved worker PID. Do not delete the journal before recovery succeeds.

## Build without installing

```sh
./scripts/build.sh
```

Result: `build/Studio Pair.app`. Native host architecture only. The deployment target is macOS 14.2. Building does not start the app, request permissions, or change audio.

## Agent instructions

Read `AGENTS.md`. Preserve existing sound defaults and settings. Do not bypass macOS security prompts, install drivers, restart CoreAudio or run test tones just to install. Report waiting/permission states honestly. An installed app is not proof that Spotify is being routed; confirm the menu says **Stereo active** while music plays.

# Studio Pair

Native macOS utility: Rust real-time audio engine, Objective-C CoreAudio bridge, Swift/AppKit menu bar.

- Keep the audio callback allocation-free, lock-free, and free of I/O.
- Never change default input/output devices or hardware sample rates.
- Journal secondary volume/mute before writing; restore only values still owned by this app.
- Keep rollback and crash recovery working. Do not install a HAL driver or restart CoreAudio.
- Use native AppKit controls. Keep product UI concise.
- Run cargo fmt --check, cargo test, cargo clippy -- -D warnings, and ./scripts/build.sh.
- Hardware checks play a quiet tone and require two Studio Displays. Run them only when explicitly authorized and with the app stopped.
- Do not publish local diagnostics, device UIDs, process inventories, or audio.

# Audio and recovery

`app/App.swift` owns the menu bar, preferences, login registration and worker lifecycle. It waits for two Studio Displays, a Studio Display default output and an active Spotify audio process. One app lock prevents duplicate controllers. A worker lock prevents competing routes that share a journal.

`src/bridge.m` identifies Spotify's CoreAudio processes and creates a private device-stream tap. A private aggregate includes the two physical endpoints and that tap. It reads back the aggregate's subdevice order, privacy, stacking and secondary drift correction before starting. The tap starts unmuted; callback and nonzero-input checks must pass before direct Spotify output is muted while tapped.

`src/main.rs` validates the buffers, duplicates input L to the first display's front pair and input R to the second display's front pair, and clears unused channels. The callback performs no allocation, file I/O or locking. Gain ramps toward 0.5 (-6 dB); nonfinite values become zero and samples are bounded. It is a stereo router, not an Atmos decoder, equalizer or acoustic calibration system.

The default output remains physical. Volume and mute on that display are mirrored to the secondary every ~100 ms. The secondary's original values and the intended write are saved atomically before mutation. Restoration uses stable device UID and restores only controls still matching the app's last write; a secondary that became the default output is left alone. User changes to the primary remain intact.

Normal stop fades the routed signal down, unmutes/destroys the tap and restores owned controls. Worker/parent watchdogs release stalled private routes; the GUI restores the journal after worker exit. Recovery identifies a live process by PID, executable path and process start timestamp. Completed journals never signal a saved PID. A disconnected secondary may need reconnection before restoration can finish; new routing waits for recovery.

Sleep stops the worker; wake and Spotify launch/termination trigger readiness checks. These paths exist but need broader hardware validation. Failures back off instead of repeatedly taking over audio. A process tap excludes unrelated application audio; sharing the physical display volume still affects everything playing on that endpoint.

## Local data

Preferences contain pairing enabled and the left display UID. Runtime files live under `~/Library/Application Support/StudioPair` with a private directory and restricted file modes: rollback journal, status, locks and bounded event logs. Logs record state and levels, never audio samples. No network client or telemetry is included. Do not publish these files; the `inspect` CLI also prints process and device identities.

#!/bin/bash
set -euo pipefail
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."
export MACOSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET=14.2
cargo build --release --locked
destination="${STUDIO_PAIR_BUILD_DEST:-$PWD/build/Studio Pair.app}"
mkdir -p "$destination/Contents/MacOS"
cp target/release/studio-pair-engine "$destination/Contents/MacOS/studio-pair-engine"
cp Info.plist "$destination/Contents/Info.plist"
swiftc -O -swift-version 5 -target "$(uname -m)-apple-macosx14.2" app/App.swift -o "$destination/Contents/MacOS/StudioPair" -framework AppKit -framework ServiceManagement
codesign --force --sign - --identifier com.browseruse.studiopair.engine "$destination/Contents/MacOS/studio-pair-engine"
codesign --force --sign - "$destination"
codesign --verify --deep --strict "$destination"
printf 'Built %s\n' "$destination"
